notes: War Memorial Board of Trustees' annual reports to the Mayor (San Francisco Public Library scans): 1939-46 and 1947 presidents' reports, the 1963-78 statements of activities, the 1978-79 to 1983-84 reports, 1998-99 and 2011-12; and the 1965 SOM / Wurster, Bernardi & Emmons rehabilitation report. Read for the Opera House, Veterans Building, Herbst Theatre, Davies Symphony Hall and Zellerbach Rehearsal Hall. The 1939-46 reports' building news (UN Conference, floodlighting plans) is already on the page or never built.

coverage.remaining: Reports for 1948-62, 1984-98 and 1999-2011 are not on the Internet Archive.

findings.address_as_written: the Veterans' Building, and the Opera House
findings.description: Two bronze plaques presented to the city by the United States Department of State, commemorating the United Nations Conference on International Organization that met in the Opera House and the Veterans Building from 25 April to 26 June 1945, were placed in the two buildings and unveiled on 30 December 1947 before consular representatives of the fifty nations that took part.

citation.label: San Francisco War Memorial Board of Trustees, annual report to the Mayor, 1948-01-08

resolution.method: The report names the War Memorial building (Opera House, Veterans Building, Davies Symphony Hall, Zellerbach Rehearsal Hall); placed on its parcel page.

findings.address_as_written: the Veterans Memorial Building and Opera House
findings.description: Skidmore, Owings & Merrill and Wurster, Bernardi & Emmons, engaged by the War Memorial trustees on 1 October 1964 to survey the Opera House and the Veterans Building, reported on 1 February 1965 that both buildings should be rehabilitated and modernized, and that a new music hall with a garage should be built across Franklin Street.

citation.label: San Francisco War Memorial Board of Trustees, annual report to the Mayor, 1965-09-03

resolution.method: The report names the War Memorial building (Opera House, Veterans Building, Davies Symphony Hall, Zellerbach Rehearsal Hall); placed on its parcel page.

findings.description: New offices for the Opera's production centre were built on the north side of the Opera House, backstage, and the dressing rooms on the south side were restored to their original use; the War Memorial's architects for the work were Skidmore, Owings & Merrill.

citation.label: San Francisco War Memorial Board of Trustees, annual report to the Mayor, 1968-09-10

resolution.method: The report names the War Memorial building (Opera House, Veterans Building, Davies Symphony Hall, Zellerbach Rehearsal Hall); placed on its parcel page.

findings.address_as_written: Opera House; Veterans' Building, Rooms 107 and 108
findings.description: The San Francisco Opera Association finished moving from the south to the north side of the Opera House, into offices three times the size of its old ones, and the Symphony Association moved into Rooms 107 and 108 of the Veterans Building, renovated with a $20,000 gift to the city.

citation.label: San Francisco War Memorial Board of Trustees, annual report to the Mayor, 1969-09-29

resolution.method: The report names the War Memorial building (Opera House, Veterans Building, Davies Symphony Hall, Zellerbach Rehearsal Hall); placed on its parcel page.

findings.description: New carpet was laid through the whole balcony and balcony circle of the Opera House, replacing the original carpet of 1932, worn bare.

resolution.method: The report names the War Memorial building (Opera House, Veterans Building, Davies Symphony Hall, Zellerbach Rehearsal Hall); placed on its parcel page.

findings.address_as_written: third floor of the Veterans' Building
findings.description: The third floor of the Veterans Building, which had held veterans' meeting rooms and a library, was remodelled for the Museum of Art's offices and children's art classrooms, and the museum, at its own cost, divided the veterans' clubroom on the second floor into a meeting hall and a clubroom.

citation.label: San Francisco War Memorial Board of Trustees, annual report to the Mayor, 1971-09-01

resolution.method: The report names the War Memorial building (Opera House, Veterans Building, Davies Symphony Hall, Zellerbach Rehearsal Hall); placed on its parcel page.

findings.description: In spring 1976 the third-floor corridors of the Veterans Building were opened as galleries for the San Francisco Museum of Modern Art's collection of photographs, with new air conditioning and lighting.

citation.locator: Report to the Mayor for fiscal 1975-76

resolution.method: The report names the War Memorial building (Opera House, Veterans Building, Davies Symphony Hall, Zellerbach Rehearsal Hall); placed on its parcel page.

findings.address_as_written: Opera House Extension to Franklin Street
findings.description: Plans for the $5.09 million extension of the Opera House to Franklin Street were finished, paid for by the city ($0.68 million), a federal Local Public Works grant ($3.66 million) and Sponsors of the Performing Arts Center ($0.75 million); construction was to start by early December 1977.

citation.label: San Francisco War Memorial Board of Trustees, annual report to the Mayor, 1977-09-08

resolution.method: The report names the War Memorial building (Opera House, Veterans Building, Davies Symphony Hall, Zellerbach Rehearsal Hall); placed on its parcel page.

findings.description: The Veterans' Auditorium was rebuilt as the 900-seat Herbst Theatre with more than $600,000 from the Herbst Foundation, and dedicated on 21 June 1978; work had begun late in 1977, the year the American Legion War Memorial Commission gave the trustees control of the auditorium and the Green Room.

citation.label: San Francisco War Memorial Board of Trustees, annual report to the Mayor, 1978-09-15

resolution.method: The report names the War Memorial building (Opera House, Veterans Building, Davies Symphony Hall, Zellerbach Rehearsal Hall); placed on its parcel page.

findings.description: The Opera House Extension on Franklin Street was substantially finished at the end of August 1979 and taken into use, adding 38,000 square feet to the Opera House, offices among them; the City Architect certified it complete on 15 January 1982.

citation.locator: Report to Mayor Feinstein, 20 September 1979; report of 15 October 1982

resolution.method: The report names the War Memorial building (Opera House, Veterans Building, Davies Symphony Hall, Zellerbach Rehearsal Hall); placed on its parcel page.

findings.description: The War Memorial trustees marked the completion of the San Francisco War Memorial and Performing Arts Center, and the complex's fiftieth anniversary, with a rededication ceremony in the War Memorial Court between the Opera House and the Veterans Building on 7 September 1982.

findings.description: The City Hall offices that had been in the Veterans Building during City Hall's seismic upgrade, the Mayor and the Board of Supervisors among them, moved back in December 1998; city agencies and the Performing Arts Library & Museum moved into the building early in 1999.

findings.description: The War Memorial trustees finished pre-design planning for the Veterans Building seismic upgrade and improvements project in September 2010; the consultant team was led by Simpson Gumpertz & Heger, and the building was to close for the work in mid-2013.

findings.description: The new symphony hall, being built on the former Commerce High School parking lot, was on schedule for completion in late fall 1980.
